messages.subject: exporting GBM models as JSON
messages.body_plain:
Here at eBay we use GBM to train regression models for ranking functions. In order easily  deploy the trained models to  production systems we found useful to write a small script to convert GBM model to JSON and a Scala library to execute the model or to convert it to C++/Java code.

We open sourced the library at https://github.com/eBay/bonsai, which contains both the R code and the Scala code.

If other people were to find the functionality useful it would be convenient to integrate the small R scripts that convert the models into JSON  into the main code itself: I picked GPL as the license for the R portion for ease of integration.

Have a look and let me know if you might be interested.

Alex Cozzi

messages.subject: Update
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

It occurred to me that I'd been slightly awful about keeping everyone up-to-date with what we're up to.  The current state is:

We've got Terry's Cox likelihood in, for panel data and for ordinary time-to-event. Any testers would be appreciated!

We've done a bunch of work hardening the C++ code, to a position where we can now usefully parallelize with #pragma omp decorations. We've started putting those in, but the package does not yet automatically build with openmp.  Those who are curious can try magic like:

export PKG_CXXFLAGS='-fopenmp'
R CMD build

At the moment we don't control the parallelization ourselves; you need to use OMP_NUM_THREADS. This will compete with any parallelization in cross-validation, so turn that off (gbm(..., n.cores=1)) if you want to play.  Feedback appreciated, particularly from people on esoteric platforms (i.e. those that aren't Linux).

I've updated the DESCRIPTION to be a better attempt at the author list.  Apologies if I've omitted anyone - no offence is intended - just send a pull request and I'll merge it in.

We're going to work on the R code a bit and tidy that up some.  That will take us towards cross-validation, which at the moment is done in parallel using parLapply magic. Parallelizing at the C++ layer exposes much more opportunity, though, so my thought is to remove the option to cross-validate in parallel and instead let the underlying algorithm have the cores.

Feedback, as always, welcome.

--
pdm

Hi!

That sounds like it could be useful - could you make a pull request against gbm-developers/gbm?

I think we're probably going to want roxygen2 documentation, plus testthat tests that give complete (or almost complete) coverage of your new code.  That will make it quite a lot easier to maintain in the future.

Thanks,

--
pdm
